subject: Post-call recap: FintechAI pricing & latency trade-offs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alex Sullivan <alex.sullivan@fintechai.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: FintechAI pricing & latency trade-offs

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned: 

What I heard from you: 
- Workload: customer support summarization + rule-based anomaly detection on transaction metadata.
- Expected volume: ~300–500M tokens/month to start, growth to ~1B in 12–18 months.
- Latency target: P95 interactive under 150ms for short prompts (<=512 tokens) for key flows; background jobs can tolerate higher tail latency.
- Budget: initial procurement band of $8k–$12k/mo; target unit economics ideally <= $12 / 1M tokens.

Options we discussed (high-level):
1) Hosted Standard (fast time-to-value): minimal integration, streaming responses, ~P95 120–160ms depending on model; unit cost ~ $20 / 1M tokens.
2) Dedicated Reserved (predictable throughput): reserved GPU pools, can hit ~$8–12 / 1M tokens with quantized model variants & batching; P95 depends on config (40–120ms).
3) Hybrid (hosted + dedicated routing): fallback to cheaper model variants for non-critical paths; SLO-driven routing to keep critical flows on lower-latency tier.

Latency vs cost trade-offs we should evaluate:
- Bigger batch sizes improve throughput and lower $/1M tokens, but increase queuing latency; good for non-interactive jobs.
- Streaming reduces time-to-first-token and improves perceived latency for long outputs, but can increase CPU scheduling overhead per request.
- Quantized model variants reduce cost significantly (~20–40%) with small quality delta — good for lower-risk prompts.
- SLO-driven pricing: if you trade a tighter P95 (e.g., 50ms) we recommend Dedicated Premium; relaxed SLOs can route to cheaper Dedicated Standard or hosted slot sharing.

Recommended next steps: 
1) I’ll attach a pricing options spreadsheet with modeled scenarios for 300M / 500M / 1B tokens (see attached).
2) If you’re comfortable, we propose a 2-week pilot (50M tokens) on Dedicated Reserved trial so we can measure actual latencies and unit costs with your prompts.
3) Please share a representative sample of prompt/response lengths (or a small eval set) so Monica can run an initial cost/latency simulation.

Action items: 
- Alex: confirm volume and target $/1M tokens range; share sample prompts by EOD Mon.
- Marissa/Monica: send pricing scenarios + mutual action plan by Monday.

Thanks — we’ll follow up with the spreadsheet and MAP.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com
(650) 555-0183

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: FintechAI pricing & latency trade-offs

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Volume: confident on 300–500M tokens/mo for first 6 months; planning for 800M–1B by Q3 next year.
- Budget: procurement is willing to approve $8k–$12k/mo for an initial contract, but execs are pushing for unit economics closer to $10–12 / 1M tokens when we scale.
- Latency: key customer-facing path needs P95 <= 150ms; ideal is <=100ms but we can accept ~150ms if consistency is excellent.
- Pilot: 2-week pilot sounds good. We can commit to 50M tokens and will share a 2000-sample prompt set by Monday.

One question on your options: what kind of commit would be required to reach the $8–12 / 1M token band on Dedicated Reserved? Is that driven purely by reserved GPU hours or also by model quantization choices?

Appreciate the fast follow-up.

—Alex
Alex Sullivan
Head of Product, Integrations | FintechAI
alex.sullivan@fintechai.com

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: FintechAI pricing & latency trade-offs

Great questions — answering inline and adding a suggested pilot/MAP cadence.

Alex — short answers first: 
- To hit ~$8–12 / 1M tokens you typically need a combination of reserved capacity (committed monthly GPU hours) plus model quantization/selection. Reserved capacity drives the majority of the price drop because it guarantees utilization and lets us allocate bigger batches without risk of noisy neighbors. Quantized variants (8-bit/4-bit) compound the savings; expect ~20–35% additional reduction depending on model and eval.

More detail: 
- Reserved commit sizes: for your projected 300–500M tokens/mo, our model suggests a monthly GPU commit in the low-to-mid hundreds of GPU-hours on an optimized instance. That maps to pricing that asymptotically approaches the $8–12 / 1M tokens band. We’ll model exact numbers in the attached spreadsheet for your prompt mix.
- Trade-offs: tighter P95 (<=50–80ms) is easier with fewer batching and larger dedicated pools (higher cost). If you accept ~120–150ms P95, we can increase batching and reach lower $/1M tokens.
- Streaming: for your short interactive flows (<=512 tokens), streaming is helpful to improve perceived latency. It doesn’t always increase raw compute cost materially, but it does change how we route and schedule — there’s an operational trade-off vs maximum throughput.

Suggested pilot/MAP: 
- Week 0: MAP sign-off (scope & success metrics) + SSO & limited-data onboarding.
- Week 1: Deploy dedicated trial pool for your eval prompts (50M tokens), Monica runs cost/latency tracking and flags model/quantization candidates.
- Week 2: Iterate batching/stream settings, run A/B for streaming vs batch for the interactive path, deliver pilot report with recommended config and expected $/1M token at scale.

Next steps (please confirm): 
1) You confirm the pilot sample delivery timeline (you said by Monday).
2) I’ll schedule the kickoff (Dylan will own provisioning) and share the MAP + pricing scenarios Monday morning.

—Marissa
